newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-ENGQUIST EMERGES FROM NOWHERE TO WIN GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-ENGQUIST EMERGES FROM NOWHERE TO WIN GOLD.

text.p: Sweden's Russian-born high hurdler Ludmila Engquist added the world title to her Olympic gold when she emerged from nowhere to win the 100 hurdles final on Sunday.
Last year Engquist became the first woman representing Sweden to win an Olympic title when she won the 100 hurdles gold in Atlanta.
On Sunday, Engquist clocked 12.50 seconds ahead of Bulgarian Svetla Dimitrova who took the silver in 12.58. Commonwealth champion Michelle Freeman of Jamaica won bronze in 12.61.
Engquist, the 1991 world champion, married her agent Johan Engquist, and became a Swedish citizen in June 1996 just before Atlanta.
She was banned for four years after failing a dope test but reinstated when the world governing body accepted her explanation that her former husband had spiked her vitamin supplements.
